onboarding.sub.prereqs: A handful of free, standard tools AI needs to actually do things on your computer. One click installs them all, skips anything you already have, and is safe to run again.
onboarding.sub.login: Claude is the intelligence behind everything here: every plan, every agent, every session. A paid Claude plan is required — it is the one thing AIOS cannot bring along for you. Everything else on this list installs free.
onboarding.sub.github: Think of a Drive folder that also remembers every version of everything. That matters more than usual here, because your agents will write a lot, quickly — this is how you see what changed and undo anything you do not want.
onboarding.sub.firstrun: A guided conversation takes it from here. Nothing to install by hand — you answer in plain words, and it asks before it changes anything. It sets up your vault, does the wiring, and learns who you are. You can take the short version, about five minutes, or the full tour. It finishes by planning your day.

finish.title: A few things are left to wire
finish.intro: The App can finish these itself, right here. One click makes these changes on this computer:
finish.change.skills: Skills — links the AIOS skills into Claude's skills folder, so every session can use them.
finish.change.plugin: AIOS plugin — installs the AIOS commands (Plan my day, Close the day and the rest) into Claude, from your AIOS folder.
finish.change.spawn: The spawn command — adds one command to your terminal's startup file (your PowerShell profile on Windows), so agents can open new sessions.
finish.change.hooks: Hooks — adds the AIOS hooks (the clock, your context at the start of each session, labels on text you did not write) to Claude's settings file. Everything already in it stays.
finish.backup: Each change backs up what it touches first, and it is safe to run again. New Claude sessions pick them up.
finish.done: All wired. New Claude sessions will use it.
nextSteps.title: Next steps
nextSteps.lead: Your AIOS is installed. Here is what to do next, in plain words.
nextSteps.tourTitle: 1 · Let it get to know you better
nextSteps.tourBody: Take the full tour: the agents you already have, companies and shared spaces, and a walk through how your notes are organised. What you already told it stays as it is.
nextSteps.rhythmTitle: 2 · Start and end each day with it
nextSteps.rhythmBody: In the morning press Plan my day: your AIOS reads your notes and writes today's plan. In the evening press Close the day: it saves what you did and learned, so tomorrow starts from there. Both buttons are always on Home.
nextSteps.keepOpenBody: This app is what starts the helper sessions your agents ask for and shows you what they are doing. While it is closed, nothing picks those requests up. Minimise it instead of closing it.
nextSteps.phoneTitle: 4 · Use it from your phone or the Claude app
nextSteps.phoneBody: In Settings, turn on Remote control. Sessions you start here then also appear in the Claude app on your phone and at claude.ai, so you can follow them and answer from anywhere. Your computer has to stay on, with this app open.
nextSteps.leftBody: The App could not finish these on its own. Press Finish setup again, or do each one by hand:
nextSteps.leftHowWin: Copy the line, open Windows PowerShell from the Start menu (not the one marked x86), paste it with Ctrl+V and press Enter. Paste only that one line.
nextSteps.leftHowPosix: Copy the line, open Terminal, paste it and press Enter. Paste only that one line.
nextSteps.copied: Copied — paste it into a terminal and press Enter
nextSteps.noCmd: No line to copy can fix this one from here — the message above says what it needs.

whatsnew.title: What's new in AIOS {version}
whatsnew.sub: Files stop opening by themselves, setup finishes on its own, and the App now speaks Greek.
whatsnew.b1: A new file in 03 - export no longer opens a tab and takes your cursor. It is counted on the folder button in your left panel, below the greeting with your name. Click it to choose which exports to open, or mark them all as seen. In Settings → New exports you can go back to opening each one in a tab, or turn it off.
whatsnew.b2: On Windows, Ctrl+C copies a selection and Ctrl+V pastes (on Linux, Ctrl+Shift+C / V, so Ctrl+V still pastes images into Claude). The ⌘/ sheet now lists Claude Code's own keys, only the ones that work on your computer. ⌘⇧-click any folder or file a session prints to show it in Finder or Explorer.
whatsnew.b3: No more lines to paste at the end. Setup links the skills, installs the AIOS commands, and adds the spawn command and the hooks for you, and it lists each change before making it. Everything it touches is backed up first. The next step is always on screen.
whatsnew.b4: A message to a session you are typing in waits until you pause, then goes on its own, and your draft comes back. And a message to a very long session is delivered once, not repeated.
whatsnew.skipped: You also skipped {versions}. What they changed is in the release notes.

caffeinate.lidAsk:
Keep working with the lid closed too?

While the cup is on, closing the lid won't put the computer to sleep; when your sessions finish, it sleeps. Your password is asked for once.

OK = Yes · Cancel = No (you can change it in Settings).

setup.whyBody: Almost every app you use lives on a company's computer — you rent the finished product and control nothing. The AIOS is the opposite: it drives your own intelligence, your git, your shell and your vault, so it has to find them first. Everything lives on **your machine**, with **your accounts** and **your keys**. That's how something running your life and business should work — the difference between a hotel room and owning your home. With the AIOS, the house is yours, and that matters more as the models get stronger.
